output.name: Lutha — The Tallow Lamp
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky drifted so fast that boats in the Leeward Reach lost their way. Hesk counted the missing from her pole and was not pleased. So Ennu the Kite-Wright made a lamp of tallow and bone and set it on a prow, to show a boat the way past the rocks. Many came home by it. Halun the Full Beak, up in the north, watched them come in. One did not. Its lamp was still burning when the wind took the boat, and it burns still, low on the Upper Sea, where the mast leans and a torn streamer flies. Mivalun, the Unflown Kite, hangs a little west of it, sewn with Aun's own sinew, and does not look down. Vesket, the salt ketch to the east, broke on the reef when Tavo came up under her laughing. Tavo laughs at this lamp every night. Sil has watched it too and says nothing, which is how she says she hopes. Keep your wick trimmed, and keep your hands on the rope.
output.finding: Find Mivalun, the Unflown Kite, low in the Leeward Reach, and Lutha lies a fist and a little more to its east, where the sky is lowest.
